candidate.name: SELECTOR_GUARDED_OR_MERGE
candidate.definition: Introduce fresh selector s. Guard each clause C of A as (s OR C) and each clause D of B as (not s OR D).
candidate.exact_semantics: Setting s=0 activates A and disables B; setting s=1 activates B and disables A. Therefore SAT(M_s(A,B)) iff SAT(A) OR SAT(B).

shannon_reconstruction_theorem.statement: For A=F[v=0] and B=F[v=1], M_s(A,B) represents the same Boolean function as F after renaming v to s, modulo ordinary cofactor simplifications.
shannon_reconstruction_theorem.proof: For every assignment alpha to the remaining variables, M_s(0,alpha)=F(0,alpha) and M_s(1,alpha)=F(1,alpha). Hence the truth tables agree under v<->s.
shannon_reconstruction_theorem.effect: The selector merge does not eliminate the branch degree of freedom; it reifies it as a fresh variable.

selector_free_cnf_projection_theorem.statement: Exact existential elimination of a CNF variable x back into CNF is Davis-Putnam elimination: retain clauses not containing x; for every x-clause (x OR C) and every not-x-clause (not x OR D), add the non-tautological resolvent (C OR D); then delete all clauses containing x or not x.
selector_free_cnf_projection_theorem.semantics: The resulting CNF is equivalent to existentially quantifying x from the original CNF and is satisfiable iff the original CNF is satisfiable.
selector_free_cnf_projection_theorem.single_step_cost: At most quadratic in the current clause count for one variable elimination, hence polynomial in the current state size.

published_unconditional_dp_barrier.source: G. S. Tseitin, On the complexity of derivation in propositional calculus / On the complexity of regular resolution and the Davis-Putnam procedure lineage; TCS 4(1), 1977, 23-46, DOI 10.1016/0304-3975(77)90054-8
published_unconditional_dp_barrier.statement_used: There are infinitely many contradictory CNF formulas on n variables for which the Davis-Putnam procedure generates 2^{c n} distinct clauses for some c>0 for every variable elimination order.
published_unconditional_dp_barrier.effect: Repeated exact selector-free projection within ordinary CNF cannot have a universal polynomial live-state/total-work bound, even when the elimination order is chosen optimally within the Davis-Putnam model.
published_unconditional_dp_barrier.scope: This is a route-specific unconditional lower bound for Davis-Putnam/regular-resolution-style CNF elimination. It is not a lower bound for all SAT algorithms or all possible SAT-sufficient representations.

rank_effect.reason: Selector reconstruction restores exactly the eliminated binary choice. Projecting that choice away inside CNF returns to Davis-Putnam elimination, whose repeated state can be exponentially large on an infinite hard family.
rank_effect.consequence: Neither keeping the selector nor eliminating it by exact CNF projection supplies the required universal polynomial single-state descent.

next_admissible_math.question: Can one retain exact SAT semantics while eliminating branch choice in a representation weaker than full Boolean-function compilation and stronger than ordinary CNF, with polynomial live state, polynomial charged update cost, strict rank descent, and polynomial terminal evaluation?
forbidden: relabeling Davis-Putnam/resolution as a new projection
using selector variables while claiming the branch disappeared
counting only variable decrease while ignoring clause/state blowup
claiming a lower bound for all SAT algorithms from the DP lower bound
